For 2 people:

  • 2 medium duck breasts (skin and fat on, brought to room temperature)
  • 2 portions1 of fingerlings potatoes, cut in half lengthwise (can be par-boiled for faster frying)
  • 1 cup of snow peas or sugar snap peas
  • 1 cup of enoki or other small mushroom, washed
  • Sweet soy sauce

Cooking instructions:

  1. Slice a grid/diamond pattern through the skin of the duck and into the subcutaneous fat (but not as deep as the meat). This will allow the fat to render out during cooking and the skin to crisp. I recommend a very sharp knife for this.
  2. Pat the breasts dry and season with a bit of salt, place in a cold metal skillet/pan and put on a medium-high burner. As the fat renders it should sound like bacon frying. When the frying dies down, give them a quick flip over to sear the underside of the breasts, and remove to rest.
  3. Blanch the snow/snap peas in boiling water to bring their colour out.
  4. Reduce the sweet soy sauce into a glaze in a small sauce pot.
  5. Add potatoes to the rendered duck fat in your pan and fry until delicious. Remove and season.
  6. If there's no fat left in the pan from frying the potatoes, add a bit of oil. Sauté the peas and mushrooms, season with salt and pepper, and add some of the sweet soy glaze.
  7. (optional) glaze the duck with a bit of the sweet soy glaze.
  8. Slice the duck breasts on the bias into strips after it has rested for several minutes.
  9. For plating, lay down a bed of the potatoes, mushrooms and peas and place the sliced duck breast over top.
  10. Serve with a nice red wine.
Seared Duck Breast with Fried Fingerling Potatoes and Sweet Soy Glazed Snow Peas and Enoki Mushrooms
